findings.conclusion: Best lap 1:20.770 on lap 2, from 2 flying lap(s)
evidence: Flying laps: lap 2 1:20.770, lap 3 1:20.940
Median 1:20.855, 0.08 s off the best
findings.calculation: Lap times as timed at the start/finish line. Out-laps, in-laps, pit laps, laps marked slow and laps that cut the track are left out. Below 0.25 s standard deviation is called consistent, above 0.6 s loose.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence)

findings.recommendation: Run more laps before comparing lap times: one or two laps do not show how repeatable the pace is.
findings.interpretation: Best lap 1:20.770 on lap 2, from 2 flying lap(s)

findings.conclusion: Estimate: the best pass through every corner adds up to within 0.00 s of the best lap
evidence: Fastest pass through each of the 9 corner zones, added together: 1:20.770, 0.000 s under the best lap
Built from lap 2 (9 corners: T2, T8, T1, T6, T3, T4, T5, T7 and T9)
Where the gap is, against the best lap:
The best lap is already the fastest pass in T2, T8, T1, T6, T3, T4, T5, T7 and T9
findings.calculation: The lap is split into one zone per corner, with the boundary between two corners in the middle of the straight that joins them, so zone times add up to the lap time. Ideal lap by corner = the sum over zones of each zone's fastest time on any flying lap. A corner's part of the gap = the best lap's time in that zone minus the fastest time there; the parts add up to the gap. Second-fastest sum = the same with each zone's second-lowest time, leaving out its single luckiest pass.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence); a sum of best passes is optimistic: every minimum includes its share of favourable scatter, and no lap combined them

findings.recommendation: The best lap already holds nearly every best corner. More pace has to come from doing something differently — technique or the car — not from repeating what has already been done.
findings.interpretation: Estimate: the best pass through every corner adds up to within 0.00 s of the best lap
findings.investigation: The best lap already holds nearly every best corner. More pace has to come from doing something differently — technique or the car — not from repeating what has already been done.
findings.label: interpretation

findings.conclusion: Estimate: the best of three equal sectors adds up to 1:20.770, 0.00 s under the best lap
evidence: S1: fastest 31.843 s on lap 2; the best lap 31.843 s (+0.000 s)
S2: fastest 22.349 s on lap 2; the best lap 22.349 s (+0.000 s)
S3: fastest 26.578 s on lap 2; the best lap 26.578 s (+0.000 s)
By corner the same idea gives 1:20.770: more, shorter pieces each catch a little more luck, so the corner figure is usually the lower of the two
findings.calculation: The lap is cut into three sectors of equal length from the start/finish line; each sector's fastest time on any flying lap is added up. Sector parts of the gap = the best lap's sector time minus the fastest.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence); a composite of different laps; no lap combined these sectors

findings.recommendation: Use it beside the corner figure, not instead of it: the two estimates bracket what the pieces add up to. Neither has been driven.
findings.interpretation: Estimate: the best of three equal sectors adds up to 1:20.770, 0.00 s under the best lap

findings.conclusion: 1.9 s of every lap is spent neither braking nor accelerating
evidence: Coasting 1.85 s a lap on average (2.3% of the lap); 1.85 s on the best lap
Full throttle for 53% of the lap
Most coasting per lap: T2 0.45 s, T8 0.28 s, T3 0.25 s
findings.calculation: Coasting = time on flying laps above 40 km/h with throttle below 5% and the brake off. The brake counts as on above 5% of its session maximum. Full throttle = 95% or more. Seconds are samples × 0.05 s.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence); no lap-to-lap scatter in this measure

findings.recommendation: Close the gap between throttle and brake into T2 first: stay on the throttle to the braking point, or brake later by the distance now covered coasting. Coasting through a fast corner to settle the car is a choice; coasting on the way into a braking zone is time given away.
findings.interpretation: 1.9 s of every lap is spent neither braking nor accelerating
findings.investigation: Close the gap between throttle and brake into T2 first: stay on the throttle to the braking point, or brake later by the distance now covered coasting. Coasting through a fast corner to settle the car is a choice; coasting on the way into a braking zone is time given away.
findings.label: interpretation

findings.conclusion: Peak braking is used consistently, up to 1.79 g into T5
evidence: T1: typical peak 1.74 g, best 1.75 g (100%)
T2: typical peak 1.54 g, best 1.55 g (99%)
T3: typical peak 1.38 g, best 1.39 g (99%)
T4: typical peak 1.54 g, best 1.55 g (99%)
T5: typical peak 1.78 g, best 1.79 g (99%)
T6: typical peak 1.72 g, best 1.73 g (100%)
findings.calculation: Peak deceleration = the largest value of the measured longitudinal acceleration held over 3 samples of the distance grid, within the braking phase. Each zone is compared with its own best, not with the hardest stop of the lap, because downforce makes a fast stop harder than a slow one. Zones shedding less than 40 km/h are left out.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence); the effect is 1.0 times its lap-to-lap scatter

findings.recommendation: Nothing to change in how hard the brakes are applied.
findings.interpretation: Peak braking is used consistently, up to 1.79 g into T5
findings.investigation: Nothing to change in how hard the brakes are applied.

findings.conclusion: Apex speeds match the driver's best in every corner
evidence: No corner has its typical minimum speed 2 km/h or more under its fastest pass with 0.05 s available
Slowest corner: T2, 75 km/h typical, 76 km/h highest
findings.calculation: For each corner the fastest pass (lowest zone time on a flying lap) is set against the median of all flying laps. Minimum speed = the lowest speed between the start and end of the corner. A difference of 2 km/h or more is raised, where the zone holds at least 0.05 s.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence)

findings.recommendation: Mid-corner speed is repeatable. Look for time in braking and on exit, or in the car.
findings.interpretation: Apex speeds match the driver's best in every corner
findings.investigation: Mid-corner speed is repeatable. Look for time in braking and on exit, or in the car.

findings.conclusion: Lateral grip is used evenly across corners of the same type
evidence: Highest typical peak lateral g by corner type: fast 1.75 g, medium 1.64 g, slow 1.56 g
findings.calculation: Peak lateral g = the largest lateral acceleration between the start and end of the corner, median over flying laps. Corners are compared within their own type (slow, medium, fast) so that downforce does not make every slow corner look under-driven; below 92% of the type's best is raised.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence); camber, gradient, surface and a short corner all lower peak g without the driver leaving anything unused

findings.recommendation: No corner stands out as under-driven on lateral g.
findings.interpretation: Lateral grip is used evenly across corners of the same type
findings.investigation: No corner stands out as under-driven on lateral g.

findings.conclusion: Throttle pick-up matches the driver's best out of every corner
evidence: No corner has its typical pick-up 5 m or more after its fastest pass with 0.05 s available
findings.calculation: For each corner the fastest pass (lowest zone time on a flying lap) is set against the median of all flying laps. Throttle pick-up = the first point after the apex where throttle is back above 20%. Exit speed = speed at the end of the corner. A pick-up 5 m or more later than the fastest pass is raised, where the zone holds at least 0.05 s.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence)

findings.recommendation: Exit technique is repeatable. Any gain on exit has to come from the car.
findings.interpretation: Throttle pick-up matches the driver's best out of every corner
findings.investigation: Exit technique is repeatable. Any gain on exit has to come from the car.

T3 (slow): 73 m from the apex to full throttle
Shortest: T5, 26 m
findings.calculation: Distance from the point of lowest speed to the first point at 95% throttle, median over flying laps.

findings.conclusion: In steady cornering the car is close to neutral (+0.10 deg/g)
evidence: Understeer gradient +0.10 deg/g at the road wheels (+1.4 deg/g at the steering wheel)
Steering ratio from the same fit 14.0 (configured 14), from 1,323 cornering samples
findings.calculation: Steady-state cornering: road-wheel angle = L·ay/V² + K·ay. Steering per g of lateral acceleration is regressed on L·g/V² over flying-lap samples above 0.5 g and 40 km/h; the slope is the steering ratio and the intercept gives K, the understeer gradient. Only ratio × wheelbase is identified, so K rests on the configured wheelbase of 2.62 m.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence); the wheelbase is the configured value; set the real one for a firm figure

findings.recommendation: A positive gradient is normal and stable. Use it as the baseline: the same figure after a setup change shows which way the balance moved.

findings.conclusion: No understeer or oversteer incident on any lap
evidence: No stretch of any lap departed from the car's normal steering by 6 deg for 0.25 s, over 2 flying laps
findings.calculation: An incident is a stretch where the steering applied differs from what this car normally needs at that point of the lap by more than 3.5 robust standard deviations (at least 6 deg) for 0.25 s or more, or opposite lock beyond 8 deg. More steering than normal is understeer, less is oversteer. Cost = the lap's time through that zone minus the typical time.

confidence.basis: 2 flying laps (8 or more for high confidence)

findings.recommendation: The car was driven inside its limits throughout. A slide that happens the same way every lap is a habit, not an incident: see Vehicle balance.

findings.conclusion: Acceleration peaks hold up: 36 of 36 are held and corroborated
evidence: 36 of 36 corner peaks (lateral and braking, flying laps) are held for a quarter of a second and agree with an independent measurement
findings.calculation: For each corner pass the instantaneous peak is set against the same acceleration held for a quarter of a second (rolling median). More than 0.3 g above it is a jolt: a kerb strike when the simulator's surface says kerb, a bump when vertical g is more than 0.5 g from 1, a spike when one sample stands alone. The held value is then checked against an independent measurement — yaw rate × speed for lateral g, d(speed)/dt for deceleration — and more than 0.35 g above it is not supported. Peak figures in this report are held values; unsupported ones are left out.

confidence.basis: checked against the held value and an independent measurement

findings.recommendation: Peak g figures here can be read as the car's.
findings.interpretation: Acceleration peaks hold up: 36 of 36 are held and corroborated
findings.investigation: Peak g figures here can be read as the car's.
